subject: Subprocessor mapping and onshore fallback options for Starlight Health
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendes <privacy@starlighthealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor mapping and onshore fallback options for Starlight Health

Sara — thanks again for taking time this morning. As discussed, Starlight's primary asks for regulated traffic are twofold: (1) visibility into the subprocessor inventory and clear commitments around which subprocessors can be restricted to US-only processing for GLBA/HIPAA-scoped data, and (2) an onshore fallback plan in case a cross-border subprocessors becomes unavailable or is out of scope for a specific data class.

Attached is our current subprocessor inventory excerpt (redwood_subprocessor_inventory.csv) — note that a small subset is currently non-US (EU/APAC) for caching, monitoring, and CDN purposes. For the special-case flows you flagged (PHI + financial identifiers), our initial proposal is: 
- Preferred: Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed network + KMS so keys remain regionally-controlled.
- Fallback: Onshore mirror nodes / onshore-only subprocessor mirrors (where available) for critical tokenization and logging; otherwise automatic graceful degradation to a minimal proxy that strips/offloads non-essential telemetry.

Can you confirm which artifact you want as the authoritative start for your legal team? We can provide: (A) a scoped, signed DPA draft with annotated subprocessor list; (B) a technical runbook that details fallback behavior; or (C) both.

Next steps proposed from our side: Karthik and Neha will scope what can be moved to onshore mirrors versus what requires architectural changes. We can produce a mutual action plan with milestones and a timeline for a pilot if you want to proceed.

Thanks — attaching inventory now.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Strategic Account Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_inventory.csv (CSV — 42 rows, columns: name,role,region,purpose,notes)

From: Sara Mendes <privacy@starlighthealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@starlightlegal.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 10:38:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Subprocessor mapping and onshore fallback options for Starlight Health

Vanessa — thanks, this is a helpful start. A few clarifying questions from our privacy team and outside counsel: 
1) Which subprocessors in your inventory are under contract with onshore-only processing guarantees today?
2) For the ones that are not, do you have variants (or mirrors) that can be provisioned in the US within 2–4 weeks?
3) We need a draft DPA aligned to GLBA and HIPAA controls; can you share a redlineable DPA (our counsel prefers Word).

Separately, we attach our requirements spreadsheet (starlight_requirements.xlsx) that calls out logging retention, KMS controls, and audit evidence requirements (SOC2 + access logs at tenant granularity). Our procurement team will expect concrete answers on whether: (a) Redwood can restrict certain processing to US-only subprocessors, and (b) there is a documented fallback where processing never leaves the US for scoped records.

Can we schedule a 30-minute legal+privacy sync next week?

Best,
Sara Mendes
Head of Privacy, Starlight Health
privacy@starlighthealth.com

Attachment: starlight_requirements.xlsx (Excel — prioritized control list)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendes <privacy@starlighthealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2026 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor mapping and onshore fallback options for Starlight Health

Sara — looping in Karthik (serving/runtime) and Neha (privacy & compliance) to outline a concrete plan. Quoting your key asks below for clarity: 
> 1) Which subprocessors have onshore-only guarantees?
> 2) Can you provision US mirrors in 2–4 weeks?
> 3) Draft DPA in Word with GLBA/HIPAA alignment.

High level approach from Redwood: 
- DPA: We will provide a redlineable Word copy (DPA_redlines_v3.docx) with an annotated subprocessor appendix scoped to Starlight. Legal will call out where we can commit residency and where we will offer contractual mitigations (e.g., SCCs + contractual notice + onshore failover).
- Technical: For PHI/GLBA-scoped flows we propose either a) Private deployment in your VPC (recommended), or b) Dedicated onshore cluster + customer-scoped keys. Where neither is feasible, we can provision onshore mirrors for select subprocessors (see attached mapping: redwood_subprocessors_onsite_mapping.csv). Note: mirrors exist for our caching/logging partner and for the telemetry pipeline; some third-party models/tooling do not have onshore options and would require either model-fencing or disabling that integration.
- Evidence: We can provide SOC2 reports, KMS attestation, and tenant-level access logs in our console. We will prepare a short evidence bundle for your counsel.

Open items for your legal team: a) which data classes must never cross borders? b) are you comfortable with contractual mitigations for telemetry vs a hard residency requirement for inference?

Proposed next step: 30-minute legal+privacy call next Tuesday (Mar 23) or we can meet earlier if needed. Karthik — can you confirm a rough estimate on engineering effort to spin up an onshore mirror for the telemetry/cache flow (ballpark in engineer-days)?

Thanks — attaching the DPA draft + mapping.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Strategic Account Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Attachments: DPA_redlines_v3.docx (Word — redline draft), redwood_subprocessors_onsite_mapping.csv (CSV — candidate mirrors and notes)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendes <privacy@starlighthealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor mapping and onshore fallback options for Starlight Health

Sara — quick note from the engineering side. Based on the mapping Vanessa shared, we estimate ~6–8 engineer-days to provision and validate an onshore mirror for the telemetry/cache pipeline (including infra, certs, and basic smoke tests). For model/tooling that lacks onshore variants the options are: model-fencing (disable that integration for scoped traffic) or route inference to a private/dedicated cluster.

Vanessa — happy to own a short mutual action plan. I propose: 
- Week 0: Legal/Privacy call to agree on data classes + DPA redlines (we'll bring the Word draft).
- Week 1–2: Provision test onshore mirror for telemetry/cache (6–8 engineer-days).
- Week 3: Evidence bundle and SOC2 + KMS attestation shared with counsel.
- Week 4: Pilot with limited dataset (customer-provided test keys).

Sara — does that timeline look workable? If yes we can lock a call. Thanks — cc-ing Neha for compliance sign-off on final DPA items.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
